tasks.title: Scaffold Next.js project
tasks.notes: Done on branch task/001-scaffold. Next.js 16 App Router + TypeScript + Tailwind v4 + ESLint, src/ layout. Brand strings centralised in src/lib/constants.ts (SITE_NAME). .env.local.example added; .gitignore already covers .env*. Build and lint pass clean. Repo had no commits, so main was created from the existing docs as a base for task branches.

tasks.title: Build the landing page from scratch
tasks.notes: Done on branch task/002-landing-page (branched off task/001, since main has no scaffold yet). Header, hero, how-it-works, gap-check form, footer. Original palette (galvanise/paper/zinc-dust/millscale/slate-wash/verdigris) and type pairing (Bricolage Grotesque over IBM Plex Sans/Mono); signature detail is a tape-measure tick rule in SVG. Icons are lucide-react, no emoji. Copy grounded in business-model.md with TODO-VERIFY comments guarding the unverified consultant figures and the compliance categories. Form renders but is not wired — submitting shows an honest 'not connected yet' notice for task 003 to replace. Build and lint pass clean.

tasks.title: Set up Supabase lead capture
tasks.notes: Done on branch task/003-supabase-lead-capture. The outstanding manual step is complete: the human ran supabase/migrations/0001_leads.sql in the Supabase SQL editor and confirmed a real form submission landed as a row in the leads table, which closes the one gap that was left unproven. Everything else was already done and verified against the live project: server action with server-side validation, allow-list checks on both dropdowns, field-level and form-level errors, values echoed back on failure, pending state, and a real success panel replacing the old 'not wired up yet' placeholder. Verified in the browser: validation rejects whitespace-only and malformed input, the database failure path shows a generic message while the real error goes to the server log only, and the success panel renders.

tasks.title: SEO essentials
tasks.notes: Done on branch task/004-seo (branched off task/002). sitemap.ts and robots.ts via Next.js file conventions, both driven by SITE_URL. JSON-LD Organization schema on the homepage, limited to facts that hold today. Canonical URL plus Open Graph and Twitter metadata. Heading hierarchy and lang verified in the rendered DOM. Alt text audit: no raster images exist yet, and all decorative SVGs are aria-hidden. Page is fully static; trimmed unused IBM Plex weights, which cut roughly 50KB of fonts and one preload. No OG image yet — deferred until the name and domain are settled. Build and lint pass clean.

tasks.title: Deploy to Vercel
tasks.notes: Deployed and verified. The repo is on Vercel, the environment variables are set, certloop.net is attached, and a real form submission on production was confirmed landing in the Supabase leads table — which is the check that actually proves the env vars are right, since the page is static and a green build proves nothing about the form. Live checks: all four pages, the generated OG image, the favicon and the sitemap return 200. Two follow-ups came out of the live check and are written up in DEPLOY.md under 'Post-deploy findings': the apex 308-redirects to www while NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL is the apex, so canonical URLs and the sitemap advertise a hostname that immediately redirects; and the domain is proxied through Cloudflare, whose managed robots.txt prepends a Content-Signal block that disallows a list of AI crawlers. Neither is a code change and neither blocks anything.

tasks.title: Navbar, smooth scroll, and footer rework
tasks.notes: Done on branch task/006-site-expansion. Nav is a flat row of About/FAQ/Contact that stays visible at every width — no hamburger. 'Free gap check' is gone from the nav as asked; it survives as a footer link. Link list lives in src/lib/nav.ts so the header, footer and sitemap share one source. Header and footer moved from page.tsx into the root layout so every page gets the same chrome. Smooth scroll is CSS scroll-behavior on html, wrapped in prefers-reduced-motion so it costs no JS and respects the OS setting. Footer now carries the wordmark, the ISN/Avetta disclaimer, a page list, contact details, a tick rule, and a copyright line with the build year.

tasks.title: About, FAQ and Contact pages
tasks.notes: Done on branch task/006-site-expansion. Three pages, all statically prerendered, each with its own Metadata API entry, canonical, and Open Graph tags, and all three added to the sitemap via NAV_LINKS. Copy is written against business-model.md's trigger event and audience: no founding story, no team bios, and the FAQ says plainly that there is no team page because inventing one would be the first dishonest thing on the site. About covers the situation, what you get today, what we are not, why it is free, and where it goes. FAQ is eleven real questions including the ones where the honest answer is that we are the wrong people to ask; answers are a single array feeding both the page and FAQPage JSON-LD so the two cannot drift. Contact is the form, one email address, what to include, and an explicit list of what we cannot help with. Shared PageIntro/PageSection components keep the rhythm identical to the home page. No specific regulatory claims anywhere — a TODO-VERIFY note in the FAQ source guards against adding any.

tasks.title: Typography consistency audit
tasks.notes: Done on branch task/006-site-expansion. Moved the type scale into globals.css as .type-h1/.type-h2/.type-h3/.type-label/.type-lede/.type-body alongside the existing .tag, and refactored the home page components onto it, so heading sizes are defined once instead of as ad-hoc utility strings per heading. The two large steps are fluid via clamp, replacing the old text-4xl/sm:text-5xl/md:[3.4rem] ladder. Found and merged two near-duplicate label sizes (0.95rem in the hero card, 0.875rem on form labels) into one .type-label step, and consolidated three copies of the primary button style into .btn-primary. Verified in the browser across all four pages: only Bricolage Grotesque, IBM Plex Sans and IBM Plex Mono are computed anywhere, with no system font fallback, and h1 renders identically at 54.4px and h2 at 36px on every page.

tasks.title: Tagline exploration
tasks.notes: Done on branch task/006-site-expansion. Seven options drafted against business-model.md's trigger event, urgency, and the consultant-versus-template contrast; all seven are written up with reasoning in logs/2026-07-25.md. Rather than make one line do two incompatible jobs, the constant is split: SITE_TAGLINE keeps the literal, platform-name-carrying line because it has to work in a search result, and a new SITE_SLOGAN defaults to 'The gap between your file and the gate.' for places with no room to explain, currently the OG card. The other five options sit in a comment directly above the constant in src/lib/constants.ts so swapping is a one-line change while the name is unsettled.

tasks.title: Dynamic OG image
tasks.notes: Done on branch task/006-site-expansion. src/app/opengraph-image.tsx generates the 1200x630 card via next/og, tracking SITE_NAME and SITE_SLOGAN. The tape motif is structural rather than trim: the tick rule runs full width at the same 16px minor / 80px major pitch as the on-page rule, and a verdigris dimension line measures a span against it with its caps landing on major ticks. Satori cannot see next/font and cannot read the .woff2 it emits, so @fontsource/bricolage-grotesque and @fontsource/ibm-plex-mono were added and the .woff files are read off disk — safe because the route builds static. Found and fixed a real bug while verifying: a page declaring its own openGraph object replaces the file-convention image rather than merging, so About, FAQ and Contact were shipping with no card at all; a shared pageMetadata() helper in src/lib/metadata.ts fixes it and removes the triplicated metadata. Home page twitter:card upgraded to summary_large_image. Verified by rendering the PNG and inspecting it, and by checking the meta tags on all four pages.

tasks.title: Vercel Speed Insights
tasks.notes: Done on branch task/006-site-expansion. @vercel/speed-insights installed and <SpeedInsights /> mounted in the root layout per Vercel's setup instructions, with no further configuration. Confirmed in the browser console that it initialises and reports debug mode locally, sending nothing — real data only starts once the site is deployed, which is task 005.

tasks.title: Collapse the site to a single typeface
tasks.notes: Done on branch task/006-site-expansion. The three-family setup (Bricolage Grotesque display over IBM Plex Sans body and IBM Plex Mono labels) is gone; everything is Bricolage Grotesque, differentiated by weight, size and letter-spacing rather than by typeface. --font-display and --font-mono were deleted rather than aliased to the same value, so a stray font-mono or font-display utility fails visibly in review instead of silently falling back to a system stack; all such utilities were removed from the components. The OG image was switched too — it now loads Bricolage at 400 and 700 instead of Bricolage plus Plex Mono, with explicit font weights, since registering two weights under one family made Satori default to 400 and would otherwise have rendered the headline in regular. IBM Plex Sans and Plex Mono dropped entirely: the built home page now references one font file instead of three. Verified in the browser that every text-bearing element on all four pages computes Bricolage Grotesque, with no system fallback anywhere. Note this overrides the CLAUDE.md guidance to pair a display face with a separate body face.

tasks.title: Vercel Web Analytics
tasks.notes: Done on branch task/006-site-expansion. @vercel/analytics installed and <Analytics /> from @vercel/analytics/next mounted in the root layout alongside <SpeedInsights />, per Vercel's setup instructions, with no further configuration. Confirmed present in the rendered HTML. Like Speed Insights it only reports once the site is deployed to Vercel, which is still task 005. Also re-confirmed @vercel/speed-insights is installed at ^2.0.0 and mounted — that was already in place from task 011.

tasks.title: Point the site at certloop.net
tasks.notes: Done on branch task/006-site-expansion, merged to main. certloop.net is registered: SITE_URL falls back to https://certloop.net and CONTACT_EMAIL is info@certloop.net, which is registered and live. NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL is set to https://certloop.net on Vercel. SITE_URL is normalised via toOrigin() rather than used raw, because the value was previously passed straight to new URL() for metadataBase, where a bare hostname throws and fails the build outright; a missing scheme now gets https, trailing slashes and paths are stripped, and an unparseable value falls back instead of breaking the build. Verified against five input forms and with real builds using both the bare and full-scheme values. The domain is now attached and serving. One thing left unresolved by the attach: the apex 308-redirects to www.certloop.net, while NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL is the apex, so every canonical, og:url and sitemap entry names a hostname that immediately redirects to a different one. Fix is one setting either way — make the apex primary in Vercel, or point the variable at www — and is written up in DEPLOY.md. CONTACT_EMAIL is info@certloop.net, registered and live.

tasks.title: Favicon from the logo mark
tasks.notes: Done on branch task/006-site-expansion. The default Next.js favicon.ico is deleted and replaced by src/app/icon.svg, which draws the wordmark's tape graduation. It is a solid verdigris field with the ticks knocked out in paper rather than verdigris marks on transparency, because at 16px a hairline figure on a transparent ground disappears against dark browser chrome; strokes are also heavier than the header wordmark so they survive downscaling. Verified by rasterising it at 16, 32 and 64px and looking at the result — it reads as a tape rule at all three. Confirmed the browser now requests /icon.svg and that /favicon.ico returns 404.

tasks.title: Email lead submissions to the inbox (SMTP)
tasks.notes: Done and confirmed working in production. SMTP credentials were added and deployed, and a real submission delivered the notification. Implemented in src/lib/notify.ts with nodemailer over plain SMTP, using whatever provider hosts the mailbox — no third-party sending service and no API key. Configured with SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER and SMTP_PASSWORD plus optional LEAD_NOTIFY_FROM and LEAD_NOTIFY_TO; all server-only, none may take a NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix. Supabase remains the record of truth. Properties: the send happens only after the row is inserted and every failure is caught, so mail can never fail a submission; config is all-or-nothing; and TLS is mandatory, with 465 implicit and every other port required to STARTTLS before authenticating.

tasks.title: Collapsible FAQ answers
tasks.notes: Done. The FAQ is now eleven native <details>/<summary> disclosures instead of a flat <dl>, so opening and closing costs no JavaScript and keyboard support comes for free. All start collapsed, and the answers stay in the DOM whether open or closed — confirmed 490 characters present in the server HTML of a collapsed answer — so the page remains fully indexable and the FAQPage JSON-LD still matches what is rendered. Questions became h3 inside the summary, which improves the heading hierarchy over the previous dt. Getting the open/closed indicator right took three attempts worth recording: Tailwind's group-open:rotate-180 sat in the class list but generated no CSS at all; an explicit CSS rotate rule also failed, and browser testing showed why — a transform on a descendant of <summary> resolves to an identity matrix, proven by the identical element rotating correctly once moved outside the summary. The working approach swaps two icons with display instead of rotating one. Verified in a production build: correct icon in each state, expands and collapses, and only ever one icon visible.

tasks.title: Confirmation email to the submitter
tasks.notes: Done. A submission now sends two emails over the same SMTP transport: the internal copy to info@certloop.net with reply-to set to the contractor, and a receipt to the contractor with reply-to set to info@certloop.net. The confirmation repeats what they submitted so they have a record, and carries the ISN/Avetta disclaimer — it is the one piece of the product that arrives away from the site, where the footer's context is not visible. Copy promises only what the site already promises: a person reads it, it is not instant, one email comes back, no mailing list. The two sends are settled independently rather than awaited in sequence, so a confirmation bouncing on a mistyped address cannot also cost the internal copy, which is the one proving the lead exists. Verified by composing both messages through a nodemailer jsonTransport and reading the envelopes: recipients and reply-to are correct and not swapped, which was the real risk. Also verified against an unreachable server that both sends are attempted, both failures logged separately, and nothing throws. One thing flagged in DEPLOY.md rather than fixed: the form is public and now mails an address the submitter types, which is a small spam-amplification vector; rate limiting was out of scope and is the fix if traffic warrants it.

tasks.title: Header and footer chrome, sticky nav, and FAQ accordion behaviour
tasks.notes: Done on branch task/019-chrome-and-faq-polish. Five changes asked for after reviewing the live site. The footer's 'Email only — we don't run a phone line yet' line is gone; the contact page keeps its own longer version, where it answers a question the reader arrived with. Header and footer now sit on solid millscale instead of being separated from the content by a hairline, bookending the light page rather than introducing two new tones. Three corrections were needed to make text work on that background and they live together in a .surface-dark class in globals.css: a new --color-verdigris-pale (#7fc9b5) because verdigris at full strength measures about 2.5:1 against millscale, a readable .tag colour, and a focus ring that is visible on near-black. Wordmark gained a tone="invert" prop for the same reason. The navbar is sticky with no JavaScript, and html carries scroll-padding-top so in-page anchors do not land behind it — verified that #gap-check lands 47px clear of the 73px header. The FAQ opens one item at a time via the native name attribute on <details>, keeping the page zero-JavaScript as task 017 intended; it needs Chrome 120 / Safari 17.2 / Firefox 130, and older browsers degrade to the previous several-open behaviour rather than breaking. FAQ questions are select-none so dragging to click no longer highlights them, while the answers stay selectable. Verified in the browser: sticky position and dark background on scroll, one chevron per item per state, opening a second item closes the first, summary computes user-select none while answers compute auto, and no 'phone line' text remains. Build and lint pass clean, all ten routes still static.

tasks.title: Custom 404 page
tasks.notes: Done on branch task/019-chrome-and-faq-polish, alongside task 019. Unmatched URLs were falling through to the framework's default not-found page, which ships its own styles and follows the visitor's dark-mode setting — so a mistyped address on a deliberately light-only site landed on a black screen with no site chrome and no way back. src/app/not-found.tsx replaces it: the root not-found file catches every unmatched URL, not only an explicit notFound() call, and renders inside the root layout, so it carries the same header, footer, palette and type as every other page. Copy assumes someone who followed a stale link while working to a deadline — it states that nothing already submitted is affected, then points at the gap check and the three interior pages with a line each on what they cover, keyed off NAV_LINKS so a page added to the nav without a description is a TypeScript error rather than a silent gap. Limitation recorded in the log: Next supports a metadata export only on the experimental global-not-found convention, so the tab title falls back to the layout default; switching would bypass the root layout and lose the shared chrome, which is the whole point, so it stays. noindex is injected automatically for 404 responses. Verified in the browser: real 404 status, one h1, site header and footer present, light background, noindex tag emitted, every link points somewhere real. Build and lint pass clean.

tasks.title: Contact form on the contact page
tasks.notes: Done on branch task/021-contact-form. The contact page's 'for anything else' section was a mailto link only, which is a dead end on a phone with webmail. It now has a name/email/message form posting to a new submitMessage server action, which emails info@certloop.net with reply-to set to the sender; the mailto link stays underneath for anyone who prefers their own client or needs to attach something, since the form takes no attachments. The four things worth including moved above the form, where they are read before writing rather than after. The intro copy changed too — it previously promised 'no contact form that disappears into a queue', which could not stay directly above a contact form. Deliberately no database behind it: storing messages would need a second Supabase table and a migration a human must run, which would have left this blocked the way task 003 was. The consequence is that this action, unlike submitLead, refuses to report success unless the send actually succeeded — a success panel over a message that never left would leave someone waiting for a reply nobody knows they are owed. Also deliberately no auto-reply to the sender, unlike the gap-check flow, because mailing an address a stranger typed extends the spam-amplification vector noted in DEPLOY.md; a hidden off-canvas honeypot field discards bot submissions server-side while showing a normal success panel. New files: src/lib/messages.ts (validation), src/components/message-form.tsx; sendContactMessage and contactMessage added to src/lib/notify.ts. Found and fixed a real bug while verifying: the textarea's id collided with the section heading's anchor id, so its label resolved to the heading and the field was effectively unlabelled — all field ids are now prefixed and the page has no duplicate ids. Verified the envelope through a nodemailer jsonTransport (correct recipient, reply-to the sender, from never forged as them), and in the browser: honest failure with mailto fallback when SMTP is absent, server-side field errors with matching aria-describedby, and a honeypot submission logged as discarded with no send attempted. No live email sent — credentials are in Vercel, so the first real submission after deploy is the proof of delivery. Build and lint pass clean.

tasks.title: Styled select menus and a written-in trade for Other
tasks.notes: Done on branch task/022-trade-other. Two changes to the gap-check form. The two dropdowns already carried the same border, background and padding as the text inputs, but a native select draws its own arrow that ignores styling, so appearance-none removes it and a chevron matching the FAQ's is drawn over the right edge, pointer-events-none so clicking it still opens the list, with the field's right padding widened so long option text cannot run underneath. The list that drops open is still the browser's native control, deliberately — it is the part that works on a phone, with a keyboard and with a screen reader. Choosing Other now reveals a required text field, auto-focused, asking which trade; picking a listed trade removes it. The field is genuinely unrendered rather than hidden, because a hidden or disabled input can still post its value and a stale detail arriving next to a different trade would quietly corrupt a lead; the server also ignores the field unless the trade is Other. The answer is stored in the existing trade column as 'Other: Rigging' rather than in a new column: a new column needs a migration run by hand in the SQL editor, and between deploying and running it every insert would name a column the table lacks, breaking lead capture entirely. The trade column is plain text with a 1-100 character check and no allow-list, and the written part is capped at 80, keeping the longest stored value at 87. Also fixed a subtlety: after a failed submission the select remounts with the echoed value and the Other field would have vanished with whatever was typed into it, so the component adjusts its state during render using React's documented compare-to-last-seen pattern. Verified in the browser (arrow gone, chevron centred, field appears and focuses, disappears on switching back, server-side error keeps the field visible and wires aria-describedby) and by running validateLead over seven cases directly rather than submitting, since .env.local points at the production Supabase and a real submission would have put a junk row in the live table. Build and lint pass clean.

tasks.title: Replace the native selects with Headless UI Listbox
tasks.notes: Done on branch task/022-trade-other, on top of task 022. Task 022 styled the native <select> with appearance-none and a custom chevron, which fixes the field while shut and does nothing to the list that opens — that list is drawn by the OS, so it kept the system font and highlight colour. Replaced with @headlessui/react's Listbox (Tailwind's own unstyled component) wrapped in one shared SelectField used by both dropdowns; the hand-rolled listbox written first was discarded at the human's instruction. The open list is now paper with a verdigris border, the site typeface, a verdigris tick on the chosen option and a galvanise highlight on the active one; the keyboard contract comes from the library rather than from us. The name prop emits a hidden input, so the server action reads the same FormData keys and nothing behind the form changed — validation, the Other-plus-detail combining, and the email builders are untouched. Two consequences: both dropdowns are now controlled, with a shared useEchoedState hook adopting server-echoed values so a rejected submission no longer clears them; and the browser's native 'please fill this in' bubble no longer fires on an empty dropdown, since it does not apply to a hidden input — server-side validation already covers it. The chevron flip was moved off a group-data-[open] variant, which did not apply in the browser, onto Listbox's own render prop. Build and lint pass clean. Browser testing was handed to the human partway through; they checked it and merged, which is what cleared this.

tasks.title: Move documented scope from A to B
tasks.notes: Docs-only change on branch task/024-scope-b-docs, ahead of any Scope B feature code, so the repo does not forbid in CLAUDE.md what the code is about to do. CLAUDE.md drops 'SCOPE A ONLY' and gains a Scope B section, a Regulatory output rules section covering the generated-output guardrails and the eCFR retrieval rule, and stack/secrets notes for the Anthropic API and Supabase Storage. business-model.md records Scope A as shipped, describes the Scope B flow and why uploads earn their place, and adds the indicative-band quoting rule. Source is docs/scope-b-plan.md Part 1; Parts 2 and 3 are business context and were not treated as build instructions.

tasks.title: Expanded multi-step intake form
tasks.notes: Scope B deliverable 1, on branch task/025-intake-form (branched off task/024, since main has neither). Three steps: the job (trade, hiring client, platform, deadline or a 'no date given' tick, name, email), the company (crew size, states, EMR, TRIR, registered before), and a checklist of documents they say they hold. Step 4, the upload, is task 026 and slots in ahead of the send; TOTAL_STEPS is one constant in lib/intake.ts. Deviation from the plan, deliberate: name and email moved from step 4 to step 1, because the plan also requires email capture to survive abandoning later steps and both cannot hold at once. Each step is written as it is completed - step 1 inserts, later steps update - so an intake abandoned at step 2 is still a row with a name and an email on it. Skip is a real submit button so the row records how far they got, and Back re-reads the stored row rather than trusting the browser. New submissions table (migration 0002) closed to anon entirely, reached only through a new service-role client, because a multi-step write needs UPDATE and granting anon that would let anyone rewrite anyone else's intake. New in-memory fixed-window rate limiter on the submission action, plus the contact form's honeypot. Deleted the old path rather than leaving two forms: lead-form.tsx, lib/leads.ts, submitLead, the lead email builders and getSupabaseClient. The leads table keeps its history; nothing writes to it now. Stale copy fixed in the same change (hero 'Four questions', how-it-works step 1, the FAQ's list of stored fields). TWO MANUAL STEPS BEFORE THIS WORKS, at the top of DEPLOY.md: run supabase/migrations/0002_submissions.sql, and set SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY locally and in Vercel. There is no fallback - the old form is gone. Not tested end to end: no .env.local in this working tree, so no database to write to. Build and lint pass clean. MERGED AND VERIFIED ON PRODUCTION. The human ran migration 0002, set SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY in Vercel, and confirmed the checks pass on the live site. One fix was needed on the way: the first submission failed with 'permission denied for table submissions', a table-privilege error rather than an RLS one, because migration 0002 left the service role's access to Supabase's default privileges instead of granting it outright. 0002 now carries an explicit grant to service_role and DEPLOY.md carries the query that tells that cause apart from the other source of the same message, a publishable key configured as the service-role key.

tasks.title: Document upload handling
tasks.notes: Scope B deliverable 2, on branch task/026-document-uploads off main. Step 4 of the intake. Uploads bypass this server entirely - Vercel caps a serverless request body at 4.5MB, so ten 10MB files could never be posted to a server action. The browser gets a signed upload URL per file (a capability for one object path, no read, no overwrite), sends the bytes straight to Supabase, and posts back the paths. Validation therefore runs twice: against the browser's claims before signing, which is trusted for nothing, and against the real leading bytes after upload, which is what decides. Anything that isn't what it claimed is deleted from storage rather than recorded. The .docx case is unavoidably fuzzy - a docx is a zip - so a zip signature is accepted only when the name claims .docx, and the archive is never unpacked. Under both sits the private bucket with its own allowed_mime_types and file_size_limit, which is the floor a client cannot talk past. No public URLs exist; reads are five-minute signed URLs. Consent is stored as a timestamp rather than a flag, and only asked for when files are actually attached. Deletion is reachable rather than theoretical: DELETE /api/submissions/<id> behind ADMIN_SECRET, 404 when unset. It empties storage first and the row second, and lists files from the bucket as well as the table so an orphan still gets removed. Also: a /privacy page linked from the upload step and the footer but deliberately not the header, a LEGAL_LINKS list feeding footer and sitemap, both intake emails listing attached documents by name, and an updated FAQ answer. MANUAL STEPS in DEPLOY.md: run migration 0003 (creates the private bucket from SQL - check it shows as Private), and set ADMIN_SECRET locally and in Vercel. Not tested: no .env.local in this working tree. Build and lint pass clean. MERGED into main on 2026-07-26 after the human ran migrations 0003 and 0004 and set ADMIN_SECRET in Vercel; storage bucket confirmed private with the expected 10MB cap and MIME allow-list. Build and lint pass clean on merged main. Still not exercised end to end against a real submission on production - that is the first thing to check after the deploy lands.

tasks.title: Analysis pipeline (deterministic, no LLM)
tasks.notes: Scope B deliverable 3, on branch task/027-analysis-pipeline (on top of task/026). REVISED at the human's instruction: no language model anywhere in this project. The Anthropic SDK, the client, the prompt module, the API key and the prompt/token columns on the analyses table are all gone, and CLAUDE.md now carries a 'No language models' section so it is not reintroduced by accident. Extraction is libraries: unpdf (serverless pdf.js, no native binary), mammoth, word-extractor, with capped tesseract.js OCR as an images-only fallback marked so the output treats it as unreliable. The review itself is a deterministic text search (lib/analysis/match.ts) against lib/requirements. Everything reported is a fact about a file or about an answer they gave: same submission, same answer, every finding names the file and phrase, nothing can be invented. That fits the regulatory rules better than the model did - the guardrails became structural instead of instructions. lib/requirements is no longer a placeholder because the matcher needs it: twelve entries with recognition phrases, documented for a non-developer to edit, every one verified:false and reported as commonly-asked-for rather than required. Nothing is source osha and nothing may be until a citation is retrieved (task 032). Both layers were run against fixtures - first time this code has executed. PDF with a text layer extracts; the same PDF with text blanked comes back unreadable rather than empty, which is the distinction the design rests on; docx and empty docx behave; unknown MIME is unsupported. Four matcher scenarios pass their own schema validation. Two real bugs found that way and fixed: the price band said low when nothing had been read, and the summary counted the permanently-unknown hiring-client item in its denominator. MANUAL STEP: run migration 0004. There is no API key to set any more. Not tested end to end: no .env.local here, so no real submission has run through it. Build and lint clean. MERGED into main on 2026-07-26 after the human ran migrations 0003 and 0004 and set ADMIN_SECRET in Vercel; storage bucket confirmed private with the expected 10MB cap and MIME allow-list. Build and lint pass clean on merged main. Still not exercised end to end against a real submission on production - that is the first thing to check after the deploy lands.

tasks.title: Automated response email
tasks.notes: Scope B deliverable 4, on branch task/028-html-email. The review already had its structure - preliminary header, confidence grouping, unreadable files, one CTA, non-binding price band - all confirmed working in production. What was missing was presentation. src/lib/email-html.ts renders the HTML half: presentation tables and inline styles only, because Outlook lays out through Word and has no flexbox, grid, custom properties or reliable style block. Site palette by hex, and the tape-rule signature rebuilt from bordered table cells since no mail client can be trusted with the SVG. Every interpolated value is escaped - file names and the hiring client name come from a public form, and an ampersand in a company name would break the markup with no ill intent. text/plain stays the source of truth and both parts are always sent. Two content fixes alongside: the empty-submission case no longer prints thirteen expanded identical unknowns - it leads with the questions and collapses the catalogue to a list of names - and the price heading reads About pricing rather than What this would cost when the band is unknown. Reordering the questions turned up a copy bug: two of them said the categories above, which is wrong once they lead, so both are now position-neutral. Rendered both states and checked them in a browser. Build and lint pass clean. Not verified in a real mail client - Outlook and Gmail rendering is the open risk.

tasks.title: Model prompt guardrails
tasks.notes: SUPERSEDED by task 027, not implemented. This asked for guardrails on a model prompt. There is no model and no prompt anymore - 027 removed the SDK, the client, the prompt module and the API key at the human instruction, and CLAUDE.md carries a No language models section. Everything 029 wanted is now structural rather than instructional: match.ts can only report a phrase found in a file they sent or an answer they gave, so no regulation can be invented, no compliance verdict can be reached, and every item names its basis by construction. Guardrails you cannot violate beat guardrails you ask a model to respect. Flagged for human review rather than silently deleted.

tasks.title: Reference data seam
tasks.notes: Effectively delivered by task 027 rather than as its own piece of work. lib/requirements is typed (Requirement), versioned (REQUIREMENTS_VERSION), keyed by trade x platform (requirementsFor), documented for a non-developer to edit, and every entry is verified:false under a TODO-VERIFY header. It stopped being a placeholder because the matcher needs it to function. The one clause that cannot apply is preferred by the prompt over model knowledge - there is no prompt and no model knowledge, the data IS the logic. Flagged so a human confirms this counts as done rather than it being closed on my say-so.

tasks.title: Internal ops
tasks.notes: Scope B deliverable 7. Two of three parts already existed: submission notification (025) and analysis logging to the analyses table (027). This added the missing internal page at /internal/submissions behind ADMIN_SECRET. Secret posted once and exchanged for an httpOnly cookie rather than carried in a URL, where it would land in browser history, the Referer header and request logs; cookie holds a sha256 of the secret rather than the secret; constant-time comparison; unset ADMIN_SECRET locks rather than opens. Read-only - deletion stays behind the DELETE endpoint, since a stray click on a page behind one shared secret should not destroy uploads. Partial rows listed too. Verified locally: gate rejects a wrong key, ACCEPTS the real one (the human got past it to a Supabase env error, which only happens post-auth), robots disallows /internal, sitemap excludes it. The table itself is unverified - local .env.local has no Supabase keys - so it needs a look on production.

tasks.title: OSHA citation verification via eCFR
tasks.notes:
Scope B deliverable 8, on branch task/032-ecfr-citations. Retrieval, not recall: candidates are declared in lib/requirements/citations.ts, and scripts/verify-citations.mts fetches each from the eCFR API, takes the official section heading plus the subpart description from the ancestry endpoint, and keeps it only if the words in expect actually appear. Survivors go to verified-citations.json, committed, and the only thing the app reads - the request path never touches the network, so reviews stay deterministic and an eCFR outage cannot reach a contractor. Re-run with: npm run verify:citations. It exits non-zero on any drop, since a citation list that quietly shrinks would go unnoticed for months.

The subpart mattered more than expected: 1910.132 and 1926.1203 are both published as plain General requirements, and only the subpart says one is about protective equipment and the other confined spaces in construction. Checking or displaying the heading alone would have been useless in both directions.

Both failure modes tested rather than assumed: a nonexistent section (1910.9999) is refused as not found, and a real section with a wrong expectation (1910.147 against asbestos) is refused with the retrieved heading quoted in the reason. 12 citations verified across 8 of the 12 requirements, Title 29 current to 2026-07-16.

IMPORTANT, and the opposite of what was assumed when this was scheduled: this does NOT move anything off verified:false, and must not. That flag means a person checked ISNetworld's or Avetta's own published requirements. An OSHA standard existing on a subject is a different claim, and lib/requirements warns that citing a regulation for a contractual requirement is the most damaging mistake that file can make. So source stays platform, verified stays false, and citations attach as references under 'OSHA standards on this subject' - never as a duty, since whether 1910 or 1926 applies turns on the contractor's work and site, which this software cannot determine.

The validator rule restricting citations to source==osha was removed deliberately, reasoning recorded inline: it conflated who is asking for a document with which standard covers the subject, forcing a choice between dropping a real reference and restating a contractual ask as law. supportsClaim is still required.

Four requirements carry no citation on purpose - written safety programme, drug and alcohol, training records, insurance certificate - because no single OSHA standard requires the document a platform asks for. That separation IS the deliverable.

FLAGGED FOR REVIEW: the candidate mappings in citations.ts are the one judgement a machine did not make. Retrieval proves a section exists and mentions the subject; it cannot prove the mapping is the right one to put in front of a contractor.

REVIEW APPLIED. Every section number was confirmed correct by review. Three changes: expectations tightened to stricter phrases (all twelve still verify); the ALL-match semantics documented on the type, matched against subpart+heading together and deliberately not body text; and the construction scope exclusion is now RETRIEVED by the verifier rather than written by hand, narrowly enough that 1910.1200's hazardous-waste exclusion is not false-positived.

The refused mapping is now machine-verifiable rather than a log note. CITATION_GAPS declares lockout-tagout + construction as status 'context-dependent' with stable code CONTEXT_DEPENDENT_CITATION, resolveCitations() fails closed so no caller can fall back to 1910.147 for construction, and the gap is surfaced in the review email under 'Where we stop short'. CONTEXTUAL_CITATION_CANDIDATES exists and is empty so a narrower verified mapping (e.g. 1926.417 for electrical circuits) can be added later without anyone declaring a universal counterpart.

First tests in the project: npm test, node:test through tsx, no framework. Eight, mostly negative - 1926.417 must NOT satisfy generic construction lockout/tagout, 1910.147 must never be offered for construction, and confined-space MUST still resolve for construction so the refusal is not over-broad. Mutation-checked: removing the gap declaration fails the test. Two independent mechanisms block 1910.147 for construction - the declared gap and the retrieved exclusion flag - so removing either alone does not reopen it.

tasks.title: Read scanned PDFs (REVERTED - deferred)
tasks.notes:
Built, merged, and then removed. It never worked in production for one reason: tesseract.js runs OCR in a child process and Vercel cannot resolve that worker package root, so it died on every invocation - and since the analysis runs inside after(), the first real scan took the email down with it. fix/036 stopped that being fatal; task/038 removed the machinery.

Every replacement costs something ongoing: hosted OCR per page, a Pro plan for the wall clock, or a second deployable to run an engine on. None is worth buying before we know how many contractors actually have nothing but a scan, and that is currently a guess. Scans are still accepted, stored and reported as unread with advice on what to send instead, and can be opened by hand from /internal/submissions - which at this volume is more accurate than OCR anyway.

Feasibility work that should not be repeated: PaddleOCR via onnxruntime-web WAS proven to work in plain Node - both sessions load in 253ms, detection 240-364ms a page, recognition ~100-150ms a text line, so roughly 3-5s a page, comparable to tesseract and far more accurate, with no child process. The English rec model outputs 97 classes so it needs en_dict, NOT ppocr_keys_v1. Models must be passed to ORT by path, not as a copied Uint8Array. What remained was ~500 lines of detection post-processing: contour tracing, min-area rects, polygon unclipping, crop-and-warp, CTC decode.

What would justify reviving this: a run of real submissions whose only document is a scan. The evidence is being gathered by doing nothing.

tasks.title: Client sign-in and dashboard
tasks.notes: On branch task/039-client-dashboard. Magic-link sign-in plus a client dashboard at /dashboard listing every submission for that address, its uploaded documents, and the review produced from them. No passwords and no accounts table: identity here has only ever been the email on a submission, and that address is what proves the documents are theirs. Two JWTs off one AUTH_JWT_SECRET, nothing about a session in the DB - 15-minute link, 7-day cookie, separated by a purpose claim checked on the way in, without which the short-lived link token would verify as a seven-day session cookie. Cookie is httpOnly, sameSite lax (strict withholds it on the click from a mail client, landing the person signed out), path /. Stateless costs revocation and that is stated rather than hidden: signing out clears one browser, rotating the secret is the only global revoke - tested by rotating and restarting, which turned a live session into a redirect. Link is deliberately not single-use because corporate mail scanners follow every link and would burn it first. Sign-in never confirms whether an address is known; an early version leaked it through a send-failure message, which only appears for addresses that DO have submissions, so only address-independent faults are now shown. Rate limited by address and by caller for two different attacks. Every dashboard query filters on the email IN the query rather than fetching by id and comparing after. Downloads redirect to a five-minute signed URL, ownership checked by joining through to the submission. The review renders under the same regulatory rules as the email, with low-confidence items going through a component that structurally cannot print a status; 10 render tests cover those rules and needed their own script since react-dom will not render DOM under the react-server condition. One real bug found in the browser: the verify route redirected to SITE_URL, but the cookie is set on whichever host the request arrived at, so the apex/www split in DEPLOY.md would have meant signing in and arriving signed out - it now resolves against the incoming origin. Build, lint and 27 tests pass. NOT verified against a database: this environment has no Supabase credentials, so the list, the submission page and a real download have never run against real rows - needs the same production confirmation tasks 025 and 026 got. AUTH_JWT_SECRET must be set in Vercel; SMTP must be configured or there is no way in at all.

tasks.title: Generate a safety manual from a client's documents
tasks.notes: Requested with task 039 and deliberately separated from it. BLOCKED on a content decision that is not mine to make. lib/requirements holds recognition phrases and a one-line action per requirement - there is no manual prose anywhere in this project to assemble a manual from, and CLAUDE.md forbids a language model without an explicit reversal. The three options put to the human: (a) a human-authored, versioned template library that the pipeline selects from per trade x platform and fills with company details, output marked DRAFT - deterministic, inside the existing rules, needs someone to write the source prose; (b) a structural skeleton naming the sections their manual needs and what each must cover, with no regulatory prose written by us at all - lowest risk, ships soonest; (c) reverse the no-LLM decision, which gives up reproducibility and citability on the one document a contractor hands their hiring client as their actual safety program. Note this artifact is a large step up in stakes from the gap review: the review says what might be missing, a manual IS the deliverable, and the regulatory output rules that forbid asserting compliance apply to it with more force rather than less. Do not start until the human picks a source.

tasks.title: HTML half for the sign-in email
tasks.notes: On branch task/041-sign-in-email. The sign-in email now uses the same shell as the review, confirmation and explainer emails - dark masthead with the tape-rule mark, tick rule, verdigris button, site palette by hex, presentation tables and inline styles. This reverses the plain-text-only decision from 039 and the reasoning is recorded rather than deleted: a gateway that rewrites links rewrites both parts of a multipart message, so plain text bought nothing there, and the burn-the-token argument does not apply because this token is deliberately not single-use. What plain text did buy was not resembling the phishing mail this structurally is, and the HTML answers that better - the destination is printed in full, in monospace, under the button, because someone who cannot tell a real sign-in mail from a fake one cannot inspect a button and hover-to-check does not survive a phone. Three deliberate differences from the other emails: no reply-and-we-will-help CTA, because a second thing to do buries the only line that matters to the person being phished; no summary of the submission, since this is the one message sent to an address on somebody else's say-so and must not confirm what sits behind it; and the URL twice, as button target and readable text, which doubles as the fallback for clients that strip buttons. text/plain remains the source of truth and both parts are always sent. Six tests in lib/email-html.test.mts - the one that earns its place asserts the href carries the token byte for byte, since a token that survives escaping in the visible copy but not the attribute produces an email that looks perfect and signs nobody in. 33 tests pass, build and lint clean, rendered and checked in a browser. NOT checked in a real mail client - the same open risk task 028 left, unchanged.

tasks.title: Navbar shows sign out when signed in
tasks.notes: On branch task/042-navbar-session. The header's Sign in link becomes Sign out when there is a session. The awkward part is that the header is a client component (usePathname, for the current-page underline) and the session cookie is httpOnly, so it cannot read the session; and reading it in the root layout instead would make every page dynamic, losing static prerendering on the five marketing pages whose whole job is to be indexed and fast. Solved with a second cookie, certloop_signed_in, set beside the session, not httpOnly, carrying no authority - nothing server-side reads it, every access decision still goes through currentClient() and the signed cookie, and forging it changes a word in the header and nothing else. Confirmed in the build output that /, /about, /faq, /contact and /privacy are all still static after the change. First attempt read the cookie in a useEffect and set state; ESLint's react-hooks/set-state-in-effect rejected it and was right - the cookie jar is an external store, so it is now useSyncExternalStore, whose getServerSnapshot returns false and makes the prerendered HTML and first client render agree by construction rather than by luck. No hydration warning. Sign out is a form posting the existing server action rather than a link, since a GET that mutates can be fired by a prefetcher or a link scanner just looking at the page. The hint expires with the session; it can still go stale if AUTH_JWT_SECRET is rotated, which heals on the click since signing out clears both and lands on the sign-in page anyway. The nav's auth item is hidden on /dashboard, where the dashboard bar already has a server-rendered sign-out from the real session. Verified the full round trip in the browser: both cookies cleared, redirect to /sign-in?signedout=1, banner shown, nav flipped back. Build, lint and 33 tests clean.

tasks.title: Loading states on everything that waits
tasks.notes: On branch task/043-loading-states. components/spinner.tsx is the one spinner - four border declarations rather than an SVG, inheriting currentColor so it works on the verdigris button and a plain text link without a variant for each, and carrying motion-reduce:animate-none because a continuously spinning element is one of the things prefers-reduced-motion exists for. Confirmed that rule is actually generated in the compiled stylesheet rather than merely typed. components/submit-button.tsx wraps useFormStatus; it has to be its own component because the hook returns nothing useful when called from the component rendering the form, and that constraint is what lets /sign-in, the dashboard layout and the internal page get pending states while staying server components. Applied to: intake form and contact form (which already swapped their label but lost their trailing icon while busy, so the spinner now takes the icon's place and the button's shape does not change), sign-in, both sign-out buttons, and the internal gate. The spinner is aria-hidden and pendingLabel is required rather than optional - the label change is what a screen reader announces, and a spinner announcing itself too would say it twice. The document download's pending state is time-limited at six seconds rather than cleared on completion, because the navigation ends in a file download so the page is never unloaded and nothing in the browser reliably reports that a download started; six seconds beats a spinner turning forever over a file that arrived fine. The two dashboard routes got a route-level loading.tsx instead of a link spinner, per Next's own guidance for dynamic routes - the shell appears immediately rather than the browser sitting on the old page - and one file covers both since a nested route with no fallback uses the nearest above it. Verified with a MutationObserver rather than by reading the code, since all three complete too fast to poll: sign-in, intake and sign-out each go label-swapped, disabled, spinner present. No console errors. Build, lint and 33 tests clean. NOT verified: the dashboard loading.tsx and the download pending state against real data, for the usual reason - no Supabase credentials in this environment.

tasks.title: Dashboard link in the nav when signed in
tasks.notes: On branch task/044-nav-dashboard-link. Signed in and away from the dashboard there was no way back to it from the chrome - the nav offered Sign out and nothing else, so someone who wandered to the FAQ had to know the URL or go round through sign-in, which would have bounced them to the dashboard anyway. Nav is now About/FAQ/Contact | Dashboard, Sign out when signed in and off the dashboard; on /dashboard both stay hidden as in 042, since that page's own bar carries the email and a sign-out rendered from the real session. prefetch={false} on the link because /dashboard is dynamic and behind a session - prefetching would run a JWT check and a Supabase query for every signed-in visitor who merely hovered the nav on a marketing page. The account links are now separate <li>s rather than one holding a link and a form. IMPORTANT, and only measurement caught it: the fifth item broke the header at phone width. The <ul> had no flex-wrap, four items fit a 375px screen by luck, five did not, and the list ran 29px past the nav's own padding with Sign out pinned against the screen edge - while the document reported no horizontal overflow at all, so the usual check said everything was fine. Fixed with flex-wrap plus justify-end: ul right edge now 351 against a content edge of 351, Sign out wraps to a second right-aligned row, desktop stays one row. No horizontal scrollbar is not the same as fits. Verified signed out and signed in on /faq, no console errors, build, lint and 33 tests clean. Not seen on screen: the nav as it renders on /dashboard itself, since there are no Supabase credentials here and the route redirects without a real session.
